templates.edit: Repaint this image as a hand-painted background painting for a traditional animated film, made with opaque poster colors on paper. Keep the room layout, camera angle, and furniture positions. Lighting is the most important part of this painting and should feel natural and beautiful. Late-afternoon sun enters through the left window and lays warm, soft-edged, window-shaped patches of light across the floor, the counter top, and the lower shelves, catching the edges of the objects it touches. Where sunlight passes through glass jars, thin leaves, and the cloth curtain, they glow warmly from behind. In the slightly dusty air near the window, a single faint, soft shaft of sunlight is barely visible, running in the same direction as the sun. Light bounces off the wooden floor and gives the undersides of the shelves and the ceiling a warm reflected tint. Areas away from the window fall into calm, cool blue-green shade with gentle gradations, never black. Keep a clear contrast between the warm sunlit patches and the cool shade; all cast shadows point away from the window. Keep the shelves lived-in but tidy: objects grouped in small clusters of three to five with clear space between groups, about a quarter of each shelf left empty, every object an ordinary recognizable item from an old small-town curio shop (glass jars with plain blank paper labels, tin boxes, ceramic pots, a few books, dried herb bundles, a small brass scale, rattan baskets, wooden drawers with brass pulls). Reduce the wisteria to a single branch near the window. Remove all ornate gold filigree, carved ornaments, glowing crystals, and sparkles. Concentrate fine detail around the counter and the middle shelves; paint the walls, ceiling, and corners more loosely with visible brush strokes and soft edges. Muted warm palette balanced with sage green and dusty teal. Keep the right third of the image calm with low detail. No text, no letters, no people. No bloom or halo around light sources, no multiple light rays, no sparkles or twinkles, no objects glowing on their own, no golden rim light on every edge, no lens flare, no bokeh, no depth-of-field blur.
templates.night: Same room, same painting style, at night. A warm table lamp on the counter and one small pendant lamp are the only light sources. Their light pools on the counter and nearby shelves and falls off gradually with distance; the lampshades glow softly because light passes through the fabric; nearby objects catch warm highlights and cast soft shadows pointing away from the lamps. The window shows deep blue dusk and lets a faint cool light onto the window side of the room, creating a gentle warm-cool contrast. The far corners are dim but still readable. No halos, no light rays, no sparkles, no objects glowing on their own.
